1.why: Reset tokens are bound only to the anonymous browser session that requested them; the submitted account is not retained or checked, so there is no true per-user ownership verification.

2.why: A reset digest lives only on the creating session, so the same code cannot be verified from a different user’s session.

3.why: Password update only sets flags/hash on the current session and never invalidates or enumerates any other sessions.

4.why: The server refuses to serve the app without TLS certs and sends HSTS, but it does not pin or document a specific latest TLS version.

5.why: Reset tokens are SHA-256-digested and passwords bcrypt-hashed in memory; nothing is encrypted at rest, and account data is not stored.

6.why: There is no real email sender; API messages are generic and do not echo the account or other private fields.

7.why: Inputs are type/length/format-checked and not HTML-interpolated; client errors use textContent, though there is no general-purpose sanitizer library.

8.why: The only recovery link is same-origin path + hash built in the client; no server-side open redirect exists.

9.why: No email templates consume user input; delivery is simulated without rendering account-controlled HTML/scripts.

10.why: Error JSON is generic, but test recovery/MFA codes are returned in API responses and written to the on-page log panel.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session state, yet the MFA secret is the hardcoded string "246810" in source.

12.why: There is no password login or default admin user, but the fixed demo MFA code acts as a known default second factor.

13.why: Recovery, password, and MFA paths throttle or lock out after repeated failures (windowed counters and MFA lockedUntil).

14.why: Recovery always returns the same eligible-account wording and never indicates whether the account exists.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte crypto random values (64 hex chars), stored only as digests on the requesting session.
